newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares seen banking on budget reliefs.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares seen banking on budget reliefs.

text.p: Hope rather than harsh reality will keep Indian stocks alive this week as parliament debates the proposed budget for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), delayed by national elections and a new government, brokers said on Sunday.
"The market will stay up on hopes and expectations rather than reality," said Cyrus Shroff at broking firm B.D. Shroff. "The market always over-estimates."
Expectations of tax relief drove the 30-share benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange index up 83.21 points, or 2.42 percent, to 3,514.61 in the week to Friday.

Shroff said the near total absence of retail investors -- who have burnt their fingers in dud stocks -- cash-starved domestic funds and wary foreign investors indicated that a strong morale booster was needed.
"Mild tinkering is not going to help. We need a strong injection (of incentives)," he added.

Some strategists expect a measure of relief from the government, such as removal of double taxation on company dividends. Under present law, investors have to pay taxes on dividends which are paid from taxed profits of companies.

"This could give the market a major push upwards," said Hitesh Fozdar at brokerage G.K. Fozdar. But he added that any recover would fizzle out unless measures were taken quickly to repair depressed investor morale.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is expected to address parliament on Monday, but any amendments to tax proposals may have to wait until September 9 or 10 when he makes his reply in the week-long debate, an official said in Delhi.
Other traders expect the government to exempt some sections of industry from a controversial minimum tax proposal, which they say will affect high-growth firms.
On a more positive note, nearly a dozen shares attracted backwardation charges on Saturday, which reflects large oversold positions and some traders see a technical rally emerging.
"The market has absorbed heavy selling in top stocks," said one trader. "I wouldn't be surprised if the index added 200-300 points."
